result.caveats: 1. Clause (2) holds by construction on the registered arm. Every statement of the extract source[0::7][:10] is a statement of the source, so its nearest-source cost is zero up to float32 rounding (highest of the 10: 0.000691) and no cutoff of the grid above 0 flags it. Of the three clauses, the readings that could fail are the two held-out readings of clause (1) and the foreign side of clause (3). 2. Source statements under 5 words. The registered reading keeps them (the shipped default reader: 70 ibm source statements, 28 under 5 words, 22 with one word). With them removed (42 statements) the readings of clauses (1) and (3) are identical, because 0 of the 98 summary statements, 0 of the 38 foreign statements and 0 of the scored second-article statements have such a statement as their nearest source statement; clause (2) then reads 1 of 10 flagged, the extract's markup statement ### at cost 1.161591. A build has to apply one statement filter to the document and to the source. 3. Clause (3). 36 of the 38 section statements of werg-a, werg-b, werg-c are copies of second-source statements, so the own side (37 of 38 not flagged) is close to 1 by construction. The side that could fail is the foreign side: 77 of 77 ibm statements flagged, lowest cost 0.3983 against the cutoff 0.34625. With back-translated own statements (1 of 38 a copy, median cost 0.1486) the reading is the same 0.9868. The second source is the article the foreign statements of clause (1) come from, so clause (3) exchanges the roles of two articles and adds no third article. 4. Executor's reading rules, each with its second reading in the notebook: the foreign set whole in calibration and in scoring (the wording of the kill-gate line; the scored foreign statements also took part in the choice of the cutoff; with disjoint halves the held-out readings are 0.9559 and 0.9125); the midpoint of a run with an even number of grid points (held-out reading over the A→B run 0.9412 to 0.9559); the entailment label at 0.5; the harness check; the direction rule. The notebook was executed more than once. No bar, cutoff rule, split or reading rule changed after the first execution and no measured number of the first execution's metrics JSON differs in the last one; the outputs alone do not prove that order. 5. Sample size. 43 and 34 own statements in 4 and 3 documents, 38 foreign statements, two articles on related topics, one encoder (the shipped OpenVINO INT8 model). One statement moves a held-out reading by 0.0116 to 0.0147; 3 further wrong flags bring either direction below 0.9. The cutoff 0.34625 belongs to this encoder. 6. The count of a faithful summary is not 0: the 7 gold-tier documents read 0 to 3 flagged statements under their held-out cutoff, 8 of 77 statements at the mean cutoff. 7. The flag reads distance to the source article and not support by the source: against 1 - entailment the 21 adversarial statements read AUC 0.6545 (Spearman +0.3073), and 0 of 4 statements of the information-noise summaries are flagged. It does not replace the model-graded grounding residual. 8. Pre-pass. Computed after the shipped pre-pass the same flag reads 0.8168 and 0.7277 on clause (1), and its count is unchanged in a share of 0.8189 of the deletions of supported statements, so the reading has to be taken on raw embeddings, before the pre-pass of the default call. The pre-pass arms meet clause (3) (0.9803) and fail clause (1); the cause was not measured. 9. Prediction. The second-article reading 0.9868 lies above the predicted interval 0.85 to 0.95. The shipped residual falls under the same insertions on the default call (median per-document Spearman -0.7714, 7 of 7 gold-tier documents negative); with the pre-pass off the median is -0.0143 with 4 of 7 documents negative, which the configured sign rule reads as a fall and which is close to zero. With source statements under 5 words removed the pre-pass-off residual rises (+0.5929). direction_matched is true under the configured rule: the three effects that have a direction matched and the cutoffs lie in their interval; the cutoff interval itself has no direction. 10. Files. This executor edited no file under src/, tests/ or docs/. logs/README.md has an index line for the E13 and E14 log families and none for E15; this executor did not edit it.

Scope of clause 1: one document ('source', 62 statements), one repeated text ('-', a list marker, 9 occurrences), 120 cases, 2 interior deletions per case, seeds [7, prefix length, draw]. 43 of the 120 deletions removed a repeated statement; the tie-break returns a textually equal sub-sequence in 34 of those 43 and in all 77 others. 2. The bar was applied as registered; the verdict follows the conjunction. 3. Mechanism of the misses: the returned matching and the survivor matching have the same total capped ground cost in 120/120 cases, so the position term alone ranks them. |i/n - j/m| compares relative positions with two different denominators; after a deletion the survivor matching is not always the one with the smallest sum. In 2 misses the two sums are exactly equal in rational arithmetic; as float64, the form the solver receives, the returned sum is below the survivor sum in 2 of them and equal to it in 0. A rule that leaves the deleted member unmatched needs the order of the neighbouring statements; that is a different mechanism and was not added or measured. 4. Position index: the record does not say from which number positions count. The registered arm counts from 0; counting from 1 gives the same counts (111/120, 120/120) with the same matching as the registered arm in 120/120 cases. 5. Exact ties exist here because the 9 repeated statements share one bitwise equal embedding row and each registered case builds the shorter document from row copies of the longer one. The tied float32 cost is not always zero: 0.0 in 60 cases, 0.0003452669770922512 in 60 cases. Executor reading outside the record: with the shorter document encoded in its own call, the rows of the repeated statements are bitwise equal in 120/120 cases, the tie group has one bit pattern in 120/120, the matched pairs equal the row-copy matching in 120/120 and the clause 1 counts are 111/120 and 120/120. The repeated text here is one token and is encoded in the batch of the shortest statements in every document. A repeated statement whose batch differs between the two documents was not measured; a cost difference of the measured size inside a tie group is above eps = 1e-06, and the position term would then not decide. Not measured either: near-identical statements, another encoder. 6. Clause 3 holds by construction: a fully matched equal-length pair is passed to opw_gap unmodified. 1820 of the 1840 pairs are reorder-pool entries. The 7 pairs that are fully matched at c = 0.6 and not at c = 0.325 are natural cross-summary, regeneration and tier-contrast pairs; their matched gap no longer equals the shipped gap. 7. Outside the bar the cutoff is not inert: on the 66 natural pairs of unequal length the matched gap is computed on 4.68 statements on average at c = 0.325 against 8.14 at c = 0.6 (shorter document: 8.24 statements on average); it reads exactly 0 in 35/66 pairs (at c = 0.6: 12), 19 pairs keep at most one matched pair and 2 keep none. The tie-break does not act on this. 11.
